title: The Day a 14-Inch Drill Hole Swallowed an Entire Lake

basis.note: median of recent videos blended with the niche benchmark; learning gated until day 5

predicted_range.basis: about 3x either way, from backtested error (75 of our own videos so far)

segments.narration: A massive whirlpool swallowed eleven barges and an oil rig. In 1980, Louisiana's shallow Lake Peigneur suddenly began draining like an unplugged bathtub.
The vortex grew into a quarter-mile-wide abyss. Trees, loading docks, and sixty-five acres of surrounding land were sucked straight downward.
Even crazier? The canal connected to the Gulf of Mexico reversed direction, creating a roaring 150-foot waterfall.
The culprit was a single miscalculated drill bit from an oil rig that accidentally pierced the roof of an active salt mine underneath.
Rushing water dissolved the salt pillars and gutted the mine, yet perfectly timed evacuation plans meant every single worker survived.

verdicts.claim: A massive whirlpool swallowed eleven barges and an oil drilling platform on Lake Peigneur in 1980.
verdicts.note: The reference text confirms that on November 20, 1980, a vortex created by a drilling accident swallowed the drilling platform and 11 barges into Lake Peigneur.

verdicts.claim: The Lake Peigneur sinkhole collapsed approximately 65 acres of surrounding land.
verdicts.note: The reference article states the sinkhole swallowed 65 acres (26 hectares) of surrounding terrain, including much of Jefferson Island.

verdicts.claim: The Delcambre Canal reversed its flow toward the sinkhole, creating a temporary 150-foot waterfall.
verdicts.note: The text confirms the Delcambre Canal reversed direction as salt water flowed into the empty lakebed, creating a temporary waterfall 164 ft (50 m) tall.

verdicts.claim: A Texaco oil rig accidentally drilled through the ceiling of an active salt mine under the lake.
verdicts.note: The reference article confirms that a drilling assembly on a rig contracted by Texaco pierced a level of the Diamond Crystal Salt Company salt mine beneath the lake.

verdicts.claim: All 55 salt miners and the oil rig crew evacuated safely with zero casualties.
verdicts.note: The reference text confirms that all 55 employees in the mine and the crew of seven on the drilling platform escaped safely with zero human fatalities.
